title: Residue split mod 3 for IMO 1964 P1(b)
intent: Reduce a statement about every natural number n to three closed computations by splitting on n % 3, using the period 2^3 % 7 = 1.

children.name: case n % 3 = 0
children.statement: goal created by mod_cases h2 : n % 3 (residue 0)
children.closed_by: rw [Nat.zero_mod, add_zero, Nat.add_mod, Nat.pow_mod, pow_mul, Nat.pow_mod, h1, one_pow (M := ℕ)] at h; contradiction

children.name: case n % 3 = 1
children.statement: goal created by mod_cases h2 : n % 3 (residue 1)
children.closed_by: rw [Nat.add_mod, pow_add, pow_mul, Nat.mul_mod, Nat.pow_mod, h1, one_pow (M := ℕ)] at h; contradiction

children.name: case n % 3 = 2
children.statement: goal created by mod_cases h2 : n % 3 (residue 2)
children.closed_by: rw [Nat.add_mod, pow_add, pow_mul, Nat.mul_mod, Nat.pow_mod, h1, one_pow (M := ℕ)] at h; contradiction

applicability.goal_shape: ∀ n : ℕ, P n where P n depends on n only through n % k for a small fixed k (often a power or recurrence periodic mod m)
applicability.use_when: the period is known and can be stated first as its own fact; every residue class closes by the same kind of computation
applicability.avoid_when: k is large or unknown; the periodicity needs its own induction (state it first as a lemma); the residue cases need different arguments

claims.claim: After mod_cases h2 : n % 3, each of the three goals closes with one rw chain and contradiction, with no further lemma.
claims.evidence: https://github.com/dwrensha/compfiles/blob/1745e6ced3e671bd74417548494b034eb2c87da8/Compfiles/Imo1964P1.lean#L59-L69; file built by lake build in .github/workflows/push-main.yaml on pushes to main

claims.claim: The authors give the informal plan as a comment beside the proof ('Let n = 3m + k; k = 0, 1, or 2. 2^3 = 1 (mod 7).'), and the formal proof follows it.
The same residue split proves part (a) in the same file (mod_cases H : n % 3).
No separate exhaustiveness lemma for n % 3 appears in the file: mod_cases creates the residues 0, 1, 2 itself.

metrics.how_counted: lines 49-69 of the copied file; children = goals created by mod_cases

consequences: Creates k goals plus an exhaustiveness obligation that mod_cases discharges itself (with rcases on a disjunction it would be a separate child). Relies on rewriting n as n / 3 * 3 + n % 3 in every case; if the residue enters a case differently, the shared <;> step breaks.
